meta.description: Builds and manages DIA spectral libraries as peptide query parameters (precursor m/z, a few fragment m/z plus relative intensities, normalized RT, optional CCS), covering experimental DDA, chromatogram, and in-silico predicted libraries via Koina-served Prosit, AlphaPeptDeep, MS2PIP, and DeepLC, with iRT/CiRT RT calibration, NCE tuning, format conversion (DIA-NN tsv/speclib/parquet, OpenSWATH pqp/TraML, Spectronaut, blib/dlib/elib), and library QC/merge.

scientific_integrity.detail: Tool Taxonomy citations (Gillet 2012, Searle 2018/2020, Gessulat 2019, Zeng 2022, Bouwmeester 2021) are genuine, correctly attributed papers in the field; no fabricated DOI/PMID, sample sizes, or efficacy numbers found across any of the 5 outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: No clinical, diagnostic, or prescriptive content; the Skill operates entirely on peptide/spectral data with no patient-facing scope.

methodological_ground.detail: Core methodological claims (predicted RT/CCS require empirical calibration; NCE must match predictor training) are scientifically sound and were positively confirmed: LOWESS calibration measurably outperformed a linear fit on nonlinear synthetic data (residual SS 0.21 vs 10.91), and the R^2>0.95 calibration gate correctly guards against under-calibrated fits.

code_usability.detail: The Skill's own executable example (examples/build_library.py) ran to completion unmodified. One reference-only code comment (deeplc DeepLC class) is stale against the installed deeplc 4.5.0 API; this is a documentation accuracy issue (flagged as P1), not an unrunnable-code veto, since it is explicitly marked as non-executable reference and the module-level replacement API worked correctly when substituted.

functional_suitability.note: Covers all promised library types/calibration/conversion paths; one documented code pattern (DeepLC class) is stale against current deeplc, though the Skill's own Version Compatibility section anticipates and mitigates this.

reliability.note: Documents the field's major silent-failure modes (uncalibrated RT, NCE mismatch) well, but gives no guidance on interpreting or recovering from actual tool errors (Koina exceptions, decoy-generator threshold failures, ms2pip model-cache stalls).

performance_context.note: 232-line SKILL.md, progressive disclosure into usage-guide.md and one example; no bloat.

agent_usability.note: Very clear, code-exact instructions and strong error-prevention warnings; output/feedback expectations are described at a workflow level but not per-step.

human_usability.note: Natural-language quick-start prompts match how a researcher would actually ask; strict input handling is correct-by-design for a data-analysis Skill (Category 3 override), not a forgiveness defect.

security.note: No credentials; Koina is a public unauthenticated endpoint; no PII. No explicit input-sanitization guidance before submitting peptide sequences to external services.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide/example separation; build_library.py is a genuinely standalone, deterministic, verifiable test artifact — confirmed by running it.

agent_specific.note: Precisely scoped trigger description with explicit in/out-of-scope boundaries and hand-offs to 4 sibling Skills; deterministic, idempotent example code.

key_strengths: Documented API patterns (Koina constructor/predict, ms2pip predict_batch) matched the real installed package signatures exactly and ran correctly against a live public inference server.
Clear, well-justified scope boundaries with explicit hand-offs to 4 sibling Skills (dia-analysis, peptide-identification, ptm-analysis, quantification).
Correctly identifies and defends against the field's most consequential failure mode -- an uncalibrated predicted library -- with a concrete, working R^2>0.95 QC gate.
The shipped example (examples/build_library.py) is a genuinely standalone, deterministic, verifiable test: it ran unmodified with no network or input files and produced checkable output.
LOWESS-vs-linear RT calibration guidance is not just asserted but empirically correct: LOWESS reduced residual sum of squares by >50x on a nonlinear synthetic gradient in this audit's own test.

recommendations.title: OpenSWATH decoy generation's real data requirements are undocumented
recommendations.problem: TargetedFileConverter -> OpenSwathDecoyGenerator silently produces 0 decoys ('missing annotation' / 'below the 80% threshold') unless the transition list carries a literal Annotation column (e.g. 'y3^1') AND chemically real theoretical fragment m/z values -- placeholder or approximate ProductMz values are not enough, even though the TraML converts and validates without error.
recommendations.root_cause: usage-guide.md's Format Conversion section names the tool ('generate decoys with OpenSwathDecoyGenerator') but not the field-level TraML/TSV schema the shuffle algorithm needs to match target and decoy annotations.
recommendations.fix: Add a short note to usage-guide.md's Format Conversion section: OpenSWATH TSV/TraML must include a literal Annotation column and real theoretical fragment m/z (not placeholders) for decoy generation to succeed; point to the OpenMS OpenSwathDecoyGenerator docs for the exact format.

recommendations.title: Decoy shuffle generation is non-deterministic with no documented seed control
recommendations.problem: OpenSwathDecoyGenerator's -method shuffle produced a different decoy peptide sequence on two runs with identical input, and its CLI exposes no seed flag, while every other calibration/merge step in the Skill is explicitly seeded.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's Tips section documents seeded, reproducible steps elsewhere but does not flag that this specific external tool step is intentionally randomized by design (target-decoy shuffle) and not reproducible run-to-run.
recommendations.fix: Add a Tips note that shuffle-decoy peptide identities vary run-to-run (expected behavior of the shuffle algorithm, not a bug) and that -method shift is available when exact reproducibility of decoy m/z values is required.

recommendations.title: Reference DeepLC code example is stale against the installed API
recommendations.problem: The commented reference line 'from deeplc import DeepLC; dlc = DeepLC(); dlc.calibrate_preds(...)' in examples/build_library.py (and the equivalent in SKILL.md) does not run against deeplc 4.5.0, which ships only a module-level API.
recommendations.root_cause: The snippet was written against an older deeplc release and not updated as the package moved from a class-based to a module-level API.
recommendations.fix: Update the reference comment to deeplc.predict_and_calibrate(...) / deeplc.calibrate(...) matching the current package API; keep the existing Version Compatibility caveat as a backstop for future drift.

recommendations.title: MS2PIP's first-run model retrieval can hang with no documented workaround
recommendations.problem: ms2pip.predict_batch(...) printed 'Model hash not recognized.' then produced no further output for 5+ minutes in this network environment.
recommendations.root_cause: ms2pip resolves/downloads model files on first use; the Skill's Prerequisites section lists 'pip install ... ms2pip' but says nothing about first-run model retrieval or how to pre-cache it.
recommendations.fix: Add a Prerequisites note to pre-fetch or point model_dir at a locally cached MS2PIP model set before relying on it in network-restricted environments.

recommendations.title: No input-validation guidance before submitting peptides to Koina
recommendations.problem: Submitting a peptide with a non-standard residue or an unusually long sequence to Koina raises an uncaught InferenceServerException rather than a Skill-anticipated, user-facing message.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill does not mention validating peptide sequences (standard 20-AA alphabet, reasonable length) before calling an external prediction service.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line tip recommending a basic peptide-sequence sanity check (alphabet, length) before submission, with a pointer to catch and report InferenceServerException clearly.
